title: Origin
subtitle: Why this exists, and who's behind it.

sections.title: Why this exists
paragraphs: I make a lot of things that don't have anywhere to live.

An astronomy dashboard that predicts when Jupiter's moons will cross its face, calibrated against *Sky & Telescope*'s predictions until the errors were down to minutes. Four Decembers of cocktails, one a day, made alongside r/cocktails' Advent calendar, plus two earlier Decembers I'm going back to make. A settlement generator for a tabletop supplement, living in a single HTML file. A detour into why nearly every four-digit number, rearranged and subtracted enough times, ends up at 6174.

I'm a collector of skills and hobbies, and many of them go into hibernation until they're needed or inspiration strikes. Programming is the oldest. I learned it in the 1990s on QuickBASIC by downloading other people's games and taking them apart. One of them, a planet-conquest game I remember as SPACEWAR, with letters for planets and colors for owners, slept for nearly thirty years before I started remaking it.

This site is where those things go when they wake up, so they can sit next to each other instead of being scattered across hard drives and feeds. On the front page each gets its own world, and this page is the sun they orbit. Things get added when they're finished, or when they're unfinished in an interesting way. There's no schedule.

sections.title: Who's behind it
paragraphs: I'm Josh Pilachowski. I live in the Sacramento area with my wife and our two kids. I'm an engineer by training, with a PhD from UC Berkeley, and I like learning things I can do something with.

That might mean photographing the night sky, working with leather, running a D&D campaign, or cooking something I haven't tried before. My favorite projects tend to happen where those interests overlap, when something learned for one hobby becomes useful in another.
I grew up discovering new worlds on my dad's bookshelves. I want my kids to have that same experience: a home full of books, games, tools, and things that make them wonder what they could try next.

sections.title: How it's made
paragraphs: I build most of what's here with AI, usually ChatGPT and Claude. That lets me build my ideas directly, without first clearing the high barriers to entry that come with learning to build software in an already busy life. It makes the subject-matter expert the developer, instead of handing ideas to a go-between and losing so much in the translation.
Not everything on this site is labeled. That's deliberate, and you don't need to find any of it to use the place.
